title: Cursor telemetry-driven dynamic page sizing to reduce dashboard query tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We will implement a runtime that tunes paginated dashboard query page_size per-tenant (and optionally per-query pattern) using lightweight cursor telemetry. The goal is to reduce P95/P99 tail latencies for interactive Console explorations without materially increasing upstream read amplification or costs.

Context and motivation:
- Since Jan 2025 we've seen recurring tail latency spikes for paginated funnel/cohort queries when tenants with high-cardinality filters request small fixed pages; these spikes contributed to multiple support tickets and one P99 breach (incident INC-2025-01-30).
- Static page_size is a poor fit: small pages reduce per-request work but increase number of round trips and backend coordination; large pages help throughput but can spike per-request CPU and IO for cold shards.
- We observed in offline traces that selecting page_size based on recent cursor latency and result-density can reduce P99 by ~15-30% in simulations.

Approach (high level):
1) Add a Cursor Telemetry Aggregator that ingests lightweight metrics for paginated endpoints: latency_ms, rows_returned, shard_fanout_estimate, backend_cpu_ms (where available). These are micro-events (one per completed page) and are aggregated in a short-lived timeseries per tenant+route.
2) Implement a Dynamic Page Sizer that computes a suggested page_size using a percentile-aware heuristic (uses P50 latency target and P95 tail guardrails). Rules: prefer smaller pages when P95 > latency_slo and rows_returned high; prefer larger pages when P95 < (latency_slo * 0.6) and rows_returned low, to amortize round trips.
3) Surface the suggestion via a per-tenant in-memory hint store (Redis with local LRU memcache) with TTL and soft fallbacks. Query API will accept a header X-Page-Size-Hint that overrides client value when present and allowed by route.
4) Rollout behind FF: experiments with canary fraction, AB test comparing static vs dynamic sizing, and monitoring cost/IO amplification metrics.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- We intentionally avoid moving to fully-autoscaling page sizes per-request to limit complexity; instead we use a short-term per-tenant hint to balance stability and adaptivity.
- We will not change client SDKs by default; SDKs may opt-in to send preferred max_page_size via header. This avoids breaking existing integrations.
- An alternative bucketed approach (precomputed size tiers per route) was considered but is less responsive to sudden workload shifts.

Implementation milestones (technical):
tasks: Design telemetry schema and add instrumentation to query gateway (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/PR-5421)
Build Cursor Telemetry Aggregator service (k8s deployment, metrics stream consumer)
Implement Dynamic Page Sizer algorithm and unit tests
Add per-tenant hint store integration (Redis path + local memcache) and eviction policy
Modify paginated endpoints to accept and respect X-Page-Size-Hint header behind feature flag
Offline simulation using 7 days of production traces to validate cost and tail impact
Canary rollout: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with AB telemetry dashboards
Run post-canary analysis and finalize rollout playbook
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for paginated dashboard endpoints reduced by >=15% in canary compared to matched control
No more than 5% increase in aggregated backend read-amplification (rows scanned / rows returned) across canary tenants
Feature flag able to be disabled with zero-downtime rollback
Automated tests cover edge cases: cold shards, variable shard fanout, tenants with strict max_page_size limits
Runbook and SLO dashboard updated with new metrics and alert thresholds
technical_notes: Telemetry event is intentionally compact: {route, tenant_id_hash, cursor_id_hash, latency_ms, rows, shard_fanout_hint}
Aggregator uses a sliding window reservoir (2 minutes) and computes P50/P95 on a per-tenant+route key
Page Sizer will clamp suggestions to allowed bounds per-route (min_page_size, max_page_size) configured in console-tenant-rules
To avoid noisy oscillation we add hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows to change tier
Use sampled CPU profiler traces for a subset of tenants to validate backend CPU impact of larger pages
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike completed — ingestion prototype written; can replay traces locally. Simulated mixed-tenant workload shows 22% P99 reduction in best-case selection.
2025-02-13: Instrumentation PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5421). Gateway now emits cursor micro-events to kinesis-stream 'cursor-telemetry'.

2025-02-15: Aggregator service skeleton deployed to staging; computing P50/P95 per-tenant window. Observed some noisy tenants with fewer than 10 samples — switched short-window fallback to tenant-level defaults.

2025-02-18: Pagesizer prototype PR (#5480) opened. Benchmarks on staging show no measurable increase in CPU for medium pages but increased IO for top-3 heavy tenants — adding cap and cost guardrails before canary.
Next steps: finalize hysteresis tuning, add canary experiment config with PM, and schedule a controlled canary for 2025-02-25.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Larger suggested pages could increase backend IO and cost for certain tenants. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant cost caps and abort suggestions when rows_returned/rows_scanned ratio drops below threshold.
Risk: Oscillation on tenants with bursty traffic. Mitigation: hysteresis (three-window confirmation) + tiered suggestions instead of granular sizes.
Risk: Added complexity to query path may introduce bugs. Mitigation: keep header opt-in, gradual rollout, and end-to-end integration tests in CI.
Risk: Telemetry cardinality growth. Mitigation: coarse tenant hash keys and time-bounded sliding windows; sample low-volume tenants to avoid explosion.
